pr_title: backupccl, changefeedccl, importer: log (sanitized) destination URIs
pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/86408
Epic: https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/browse/CC-5615

Previously, there were no logs that indicated the destinations CRDB was attempting to connect to during egress enabled jobs (BACKUP,IMPORT, CHANGEFEED, RESTORE).

This needed to change because security teams want the ability to analyze egress traffic coming out of a CRDB cluster. These logs allow them to determine which traffic is actually user initiated (network egress logs align with CRDB logs). And furthermore, if that traffic is initiated by a malicious user (comparing with historical logs indicating unexpected destinations).

To address this, jobs that leverage egress have been modified to include additional logging. Note that we mark the logged destinations as redact safe since we ensure to log only sanitized URIs.
While there may be other ways to manipulate CRDB to make egress calls, these jobs (BACKUP, IMPORT, CHANGEFEED, RESTORE) are the most likely targets for egress manipulation.

Release Note (general change): Bulk operations now log the (sanitized) destinations they are connecting to. For example "backup planning to connect to destination gs://test/backupadhoc?AUTH=specified&CREDENTIALS=redacted"
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/89531)

> My understanding is that the goal here is to provide a low-cost way to line up other logs related to external access with specific user actions.

Correct 👌 

> Even though they are single log-lines, it might be nice to move this logging into a well named function so that it doesn't get accidentally removed -- especially for the log lines in restore, which currently live in functions that aren't necessarily obvious would be logging.

Done.

> For the new external-connection features, the current code will only log the name of the external connection.

What are the "new external-connection" features? Are these things other than the BACKUP, RESTORE, IMPORT, EXPORT, CREATE CHANGEFEED statements ?


> You probably want to modify EXPORT as well

Could you point me to where that would be? I started this PR by finding the usages of `cloud.SanitizeExternalStorageURI` and that did not lead me to EXPORT. I also don't see an `export_planning` file similar to how i see for the other operations.

This is currently logging only in planning, right? So if someone starts a changefeed -- which would log -- and then pauses it, and then several days later comes back and resumes it, it'll start making network connections at that point, but will not log anything new at that point, since it doesn't go back through planning on resume. Is that ok?

>  it'll start making network connections at that point, but will not log anything new at that point, since it doesn't go back through planning on resume. Is that ok?

Yes that's fine, give that it is not possible to change the destination by pausing/resuming.
Another note is that this won't cover confluent schema registries (CDC) and KMS (backup/restore).

@stevendanna I've added logging around the creation of external connections which satisfies our use case (since external connections currently can't be altered/modified - if they did we would want logging there too).

I also added logging for EXPORT and backup/restore KMS.

For confluent schema registries i could find a way to easily do this only on changefeed set up only. However, like some other less common egress scenarios we are willing to ignore logging here.

PTAL

> This looks good to me! Are these logs going to the Ops channel?

They were going to Dev. I have changed the logging statements to send to the Ops channel.

issue_context.title: Log domain and IP address of remote servers in Bulk IO calls
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Bulk IO operations (such as imports/backups) have the target server redacted in the Ops channel logs, which is problematic for determining if a remote Bulk IO operation is legitimate or not. While redacting the full URL makes sense, given there may be authentication credentials in the URL, it would help security teams to determine if an action is legitimate or not if we can compare the domains being connected to (or the lack thereof).

For example, if my cluster normally backs up to "backups.example.com" and then backs up to an IP address (without a domain name), someone might have obtained access to my cluster and be trying to exfiltrate data.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Logging just the domain name (extracted from the URL) and the IP address being connected to would help us to determine if the action is legitimate or not.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Another alternative would be to log the full URL, without any query parameters, as that would help with comparing S3 buckets in the same region.
